title: Terraform module: VPC Topology Wizard — subnet roles, egress, endpoints & health hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reusable, auditable Terraform module (registry-ready) that encapsulates VPC topology patterns for Private deployments: role-aware subnets (control, inference, state, egress), NAT/IGW egress with multi-AZ failover, VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, KMS, STS), route table orchestration, and built-in health hooks for automated probes and upgrade safety.

Scope:
- Module inputs: AZ map, subnet-role definitions, CIDR templates, managed vs. customer-provided NAT, endpoint toggles, tagging schema, encryption/KMS options, and route preferences.
- Outputs: subnet ids by role, route table ids, endpoint ids, NAT/IGW status, and a small "health hook" SNS topic/SSM parameter that higher-level automation can consume.
- Health checks: include optional synthetic-probe configuration (Lambda + CloudWatch/SSM runbook) that validates reachability to endpoints and egress paths and emits structured diagnostics.
- Upgrades: support canary replacement pattern via subnet-level rolling updates (safe destroy/create of AZ-subnets with capacity-awareness), plus terraform plan-time validations to reject destructive changes without explicit approval.
- Observability: expose CloudWatch metrics and log group names for probe runs; wire up tags for Console to correlate with runtime instances.

Non-goals: VPC peerings, Service meshes, or application-level firewall rules; those will be separate modules. This module focuses on network topology, egress reliability, endpoint hygiene, and preflight/health tooling for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Module published to internal Terraform registry with semver-compliant releases
Module creates subnets with role labels and returns stable outputs (subnet ids by role) for downstream stacks
Egress path out of the VPC uses a primary NAT gateway per AZ and an IGW fallback as configured; module supports single-NAT and HA-NAT patterns
VPC endpoints for S3/ECR/KMS/STS can be toggled and created with correct policy attachments and route table associations
Health hook option deploys a synthetic probe that verifies endpoint connectivity and egress; probe failures are surfaced to an SNS topic and a CloudWatch dashboard
Upgrade path documented: terraform plan stage flags destructive subnet changes and module supports canary subnet replacement scripts/steps
Automated preflight validations (CIDR overlaps, AZ capacity hints) run as a terraform plan wrapper and fail fast with actionable messages
tasks: Draft API surface (inputs/outputs) and tagging conventions
Prototype Terraform resources for subnet roles and route tables (iterative loops for AZs)
Implement optional synthetic probe (Lambda + CloudWatch) and SNS notify pattern
Add endpoint creation with policy templates and route table attachments
Add upgrade/canary helper scripts and sample usage docs
Write unit/acceptance tests using terratest and smoke runs in a sandbox account
Publish module and create initial changelog entry and registry listing
design_decisions: Use role-based subnet naming (role + index + AZ) to keep outputs deterministic and stable
Prefer managed NAT gateway by default but allow BYO NAT resources for advanced customers
Health probes will run at a conservative interval (5 minutes) and include jitter to reduce burst load across accounts
Use CloudWatch metrics and a single SNS topic per module instance to surface probe status; avoid cross-account SNS by default
Do not attempt to automatically modify customer-provided route tables; only attach route table associations when managed by module
